AGENTCRAFT.

Building Your World with Foundation Models

How to Build Specialist Agents with General-Purpose FMs and Tools?

General foundation.
Specific worlds.

Incentize Task-Specific Capabilities with General Models and Tools via Module Orchastration, Information Flow Control, and Interpretable Self-Improvement Strategies.

[ + ]
01 / Overview of Workshop

Agents are typically building specialist agents around general-purpose FMs with predefined/recursively evolved external workflows and tool invocation strategies.

In this case, FM-based agents can be seen as a comprehensive system that combines powerful general-purpose FMs, along with test-time inference, external tools, memories, interactions among FMs, and feedback from either environments or human beings.

In practice, much like building a customized world from shared building blocks and tools in Minecraft, constructing a specialist agentic system for a domain involves assembling a set of appropriate general modules, including skill kits and tools, and meticulously manipulating the information flow around a powerful general-purpose FM.

How can we craft agents from general-purpose FMs to tackle complex real-world challenges and build the worlds we envision?

02 / Topics of Interest

Topics include, but are not limited to, the following.

i

Specialist agentic systems

Build specialist agents around general-purpose foundation models and tools for scientific discovery, healthcare, biomedicine, robotic manipulation and personal assistance. Both advances in a field’s workflow and failed cases that show capability boundaries are in scope.

ii

Information flow and module orchestration

Study how tool use and information flow change task performance, and how to coordinate models, tools and memory in general or task-specific systems.

iii

Trustworthy self-improvement

Develop safe, robust and interpretable ways for agents to refine their workflows from execution feedback, so changes stay controllable.

iv

Interpretation of agentic systems

Formulate how foundation models, test-time inference, tools, memory, interactions and feedback jointly produce particular behaviors.

v

Trustworthy and grounded evaluation

Build metrics and benchmarks that look past accuracy and success rate, including how systems handle unexpected or misleading signals and how models interact with tools.
